solution: Separate: $\\tfrac{dy}{y(1-y)}=dx$. Since $\\tfrac{1}{y(1-y)}=\\tfrac{1}{y}+\\tfrac{1}{1-y}$, integrating gives $\\ln|y|-\\ln|1-y|=x+C$, i.e. $\\ln\\tfrac{y}{1-y}=x+C$. With $y(0)=\\tfrac12$: $\\ln1=C\\Rightarrow C=0$, so $\\tfrac{y}{1-y}=\\mathrm{e}^{x}$, giving $y=\\tfrac{\\mathrm{e}^{x}}{1+\\mathrm{e}^{x}}$.
hints: Use the initial condition to fix the constant.
